title: Amazon is pushing back on Meta's new AI agent, and the reason matters for every online retailer
source_used: Yahoo Finance (copy of the MLive / Advance Local text, which itself is based on Retail Dive)
key_facts: Meta has launched an AI agent called Muse for Small Business, aimed at helping small businesses automate business tasks.
The tool lets a business require human approval before Muse completes purchases or publishes information for it.

A Meta spokesperson told Retail Dive that Muse uses single-card numbers for new merchants, does not collect passwords or payment information, and keeps virtual machine data separate from Meta's advertising systems.
Amazon last week asked Meta to remove its e-commerce platform from Muse, saying it had not consented to being included.
The move follows a legal dispute Amazon filed against Perplexity, whose AI agent made purchases on Amazon without authorization (Retail Dive).
A US appeals court overturned a temporary restraining order against Perplexity in August.
Advance Local says generative AI was used to draft this one-minute story from Retail Dive data, and that it was reviewed and edited.
